ios.desc:
A "Cade" is a self-contained super short fiction story that spans a maximum of 500 words. We embarked on this experiment due to two observations. Firstly, our current reading experience on smartphones is limited to transcribed literary formats, essentially reading printed books through reading apps. Secondly, our interactions with phones are predominantly brief, involving activities such as checking Instagram stories, reading news headlines, checking the weather, or engaging in quick chat messages. By combining these observations, we aimed to explore whether there was an opportunity to create a literary format specifically tailored to the way people interact with their phones, rather than the other way around.
From the perspective of the writer, this format presents a challenge: Can you tell a complete story within 500 words? A similar challenge was posed to the renowned science fiction writer Isaac Asimov back in 1957. During a panel, he was asked to spontaneously write a story, resulting in a mini-story called "Insert knob A, in hole B," which consisted of only 350 words. In this spirit, we are reprinting Asimov's story as our first Cade, showcasing the brevity and creativity that can be achieved within this format.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Cade – Create short fiction stories of 500 words and browse like TikTok

quotes.text:
Hello Dear HN community,

I'm excited to introduce my app, Cade.

Cade is an app for literature where users can read and create super short fiction stories with a maximum of 500 words(min 300), browse them like TikTok (swiping up-down) and read with a Tap gesture, like an Instagram Story. It’s free on the App Store, with no sign up required (for reading).

My goal with Cade is to create an immersive literary experience tailor-made for the iPhone, rather than adapting traditional literature formats to fit the constraints of a smartphone.

Here's how I approached the problem:

* Recognizing our frequent and brief interactions with our phones, I opted for concise stories that can be enjoyed in just a few minutes.

* I drew inspiration from the straightforward and popular browsing experience of TikTok, the Instagram Story format, and other popular e-readers, favoring a tap and swipe gestures over traditional scrolling.

* By setting a limit of 500 words, Cade poses both a challenge for experienced writers and an opportunity for aspiring authors who don't need to embark on a full 200-page novel to share their work.

Lastly, but not least, I'd like to build a community of writers and readers, across the world, that can enjoy some literature on the go, in an interface that’s free from distracting ads and algorithms.

I built Cade entirely, from concept to development and design.

I hope you enjoy it and can provide some suggestions on how to improve it!

Thanks a lot,
Luca Columbu
